patch_resolves_note: The staged fixed-source rebuild applied the upstream `malloc(other->keylen)` plus `memcpy(..., other->keylen)` change in `ucl_object_copy_internal()`, and the fixed original still executed the same inherited-key copy and hash path with `copy_bytes == keylen_after == hash_len == 333` instead of the vulnerable `122 < 333` mismatch.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled malformed key state. On the vulnerable path, this in-place JSON unescape decodes a quoted key containing `\u0000` into an owned key buffer that now contains a literal embedded NUL while `ret` remains the full decoded key length.

The copy path duplicates an embedded-NUL key with `strdup`, which allocates only through the first NUL. Because the earlier whole-object `memcpy()` has already preserved the source `keylen`, rebinding `new->key` to this short allocation creates a pointer-length mismatch later consumed by hashing.

ASan crash site. The low-level hasher reads an 8-byte word from `str` while hashing the copied key for `len == copy->keylen`; because the copied key storage was truncated by `strdup` at the first embedded NUL, this read crosses the right edge of that heap allocation.

edges.description: The same copied key pointer installed into `new->key` at the root copy site is the `key` argument consumed by `_mum_hash_aligned()` on the crashing hash path.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `copy_key_post.key_ptr == hash_word_read.hash_key_ptr` on the crashing case.

edges.description: The preserved logical key length carried in `new->keylen` reaches `_mum_hash_aligned()` unchanged as the `len` argument that drives the out-of-bounds read.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `copy_key_post.keylen_after == hash_word_read.hash_len == 333`.
